doc.title: Phil Flanigan interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 15, 1998

title: Road work with Hamilton, duos with John Bunch and learning from people
summary: The Hamilton group toured about 14 weeks in 1978; he began playing duo with Bunch and stresses learning from older players.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: How long did you stay in New York and did you get out doing road work with those particular — with Scott, you did some traveling?

Well I got out with Scott quite a bit. I think we didn’t work as much as a lot of people thought we did. I remember I think it was 1978, we’d been there a year and a half or so, where we had our best year on the road, I think we did 14 weeks on the road. And we never did as much as that again. Although we did anywhere from half to two thirds of that or something, for the next almost ten years. But everyone was relying more and more on freelancing in the New York area, and picking up whatever you could on the road with other people. I started working in duo situations with John Bunch. That tided me through a lot of potential poverty, and I also got a chance to learn all his stuff. It’s the people that you’re around. I keep trying to tell guys that are in school this, that the book learning and the theoretical knowledge and even the practicing and theoretical knowledge is great. But the thing that makes it what it is is the human element and if you want to be it you have to hang around it and you have to experience it, and it is the people that are doing it. So you’ve got to get out and hang out and get to know the people that are, like whoever it is that you look up to. In my case it was the people like Benny Goodman and Roy Eldridge and Maxine Sullivan and Vic Dickinson and Scott Hamilton and Ruby Braff, and Kenny Davern and Bob Wilber and those kind of people that were — some of them I didn’t have knowledge of before I moved to town. But once I was on that scene, just from playing gigs with a lot of different people and using my own ears and my own judgment, yeah, I mean these were the people.
